source_locator: R2225: ch. XI; R2227: Part VI, ch. 9

notes: The 27th Infantry attacked the Galloping Horse at 0635 on 10 January 1943 (Miller, ch. XI). Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9, independently record that Army units began their attacks against the Galloping Horse on 10 January, with final actions there three days later. Old confidence was 0.5, from Miller only. New confidence is 0.7, because a second official family (usmc_history) agrees on the 10 January opening.

notes: The 27th Infantry cleared Sims Ridge and completed the capture of the Galloping Horse on 13 January 1943 (Miller, ch. XI). Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9, independently record that the final actions on the Galloping Horse came three days after the 10 January opening. Old confidence was 0.5, from Miller only. New confidence is 0.7, because a second official family (usmc_history) agrees on the 13 January completion.

current_activity: reaching the high ground immediately east and south of Kokumbona
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: on 22 January 1943 the 27th Infantry attacked west from the Galloping Horse. By nightfall the 1st Battalion had gained over 4,500 yards and the regiment had reached its objective, the high ground east and south of Kokumbona (Hills 90 and 98). Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, Second Day: The Capture of Kokumbona; R2226: ch. IX, The Final Drive
current_activity: entering Kokumbona from the east and south by 1510
notes: Miller, ch. XIV, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that American forces took Kokumbona on 23 January 1943. Miller gives the 27th Infantry's plan completed on the night of 22-23 January: 3rd Battalion extended to the beach over Hills 98 and 99, then 1st Battalion (with attachments) sent two columns into the village from the east and south, joining there by 1510. Confidence 0.7.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, Second Day: The Capture of Kokumbona
current_activity: reaching the Poha River late in the afternoon
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: on 25 January 1943 the 27th Infantry attacked again with orders to reach the Poha. 3rd Battalion passed through 1st Battalion in Kokumbona about noon, advanced along the coast, and in the late afternoon reached the Poha area, crossed several mouths of the delta, and bivouacked in a coconut grove west of the main stream after an artillery ranging round confirmed the river mouth. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.
